info.name: Privilege MCP Gateway — SE cluster (tokenless)
info.description:
Tests the cyonproxy gateway deployed via k8s/helm/mcpgw in ping-devops-cmuir on the SE AWS cluster (see privilege/deploy-whole-stack.prompt.md). Unlike Privilege-MCP-Gateway.postman_collection.json (agentless mcpgw binary, PingOne OAuth challenge) and Privilege-MCP-Debug.postman_collection.json (local docker, console-token flows), cyonproxy has NO OAuth challenge and needs NO PingOne token, NO console token, NO client_id/secret — every request in this collection is tokenless (auth: noauth at the collection level).

Routing/authorization for cyonproxy is entirely mesh-based: which backend MCP server a request reaches is decided by policy authored in the Privilege console (Cloud > Applications), not by anything in the request itself. As of 2026-08-13 no MCP application has been registered against this cluster's node (297a919a-8395-4754-a9cd-107b8ae7b3d9) — see '0. Gateway liveness' below, which currently returns 502 for exactly that reason. Registering a backend is the one step this collection cannot do for you: PingOne Privilege console > AI Security > Agentic Apps > Add Application > MCP Server tile, Mesh Cluster = the gateway enrolled here.

Once a backend is registered, requests 1-3 exercise the standard MCP JSON-RPC surface with no auth headers at all.

item.name: 0. Gateway liveness — GET /mcpgw/ (expect 502 until a backend is registered in console)

exec: console.log('502 here means the proxy itself is reachable but has no backend MCP server');
console.log('registered against this cluster in the Privilege console yet — expected until');
console.log('someone completes Cloud > Applications > Add Application > MCP Server there.');
console.log('A connection error (not 502) instead means the proxy pod itself is down —');
console.log('check: kubectl get pods -n ping-devops-cmuir | grep ping-mcpgw');
pm.test('gateway reachable (502 = up, no backend yet; 200 = up, backend registered)', () => [200, 502].includes(pm.response.code));
if (sessionId) { pm.environment.set('mcp_session_id', sessionId); console.log('captured session:', sessionId); }
console.log('502 = no backend registered in console yet, see request 0.');
if (json.result && json.result.tools) console.log('Available tools:', json.result.tools.map(t => t.name).join(', '));

item.name: 3. Call Tool (edit name/arguments to match a registered tool)
Kubernetes — reference (not runnable from Postman)
item.description:
Direct-to-Service access bypasses the SE ingress entirely — useful when {{gateway_url}} 502s and you need to tell 'proxy down' from 'no backend registered' apart, or when testing before an Ingress/cert exists.

Port-forward:
  kubectl port-forward -n {{namespace}} svc/{{helm_release}}-mcpgw 8680:80

Then point gateway_url at http://localhost:8680 (no TLS) for the same requests above.

Pod/log check:
  kubectl get pods -n {{namespace}} | grep {{helm_release}}
  kubectl logs -n {{namespace}} deployment/{{helm_release}}-mcpgw -c log-tailer --tail=30
(-c mcpgw is normally empty even when healthy — cyonproxy logs to a file, log-tailer is the sidecar tailing it.)
